rationale: llubenchmark is a pointer/integer linked-list workload: hot loops with simple arithmetic (SUB applies broadly at near-zero cost, so it gets the highest SecurityGain weight and minimal cost weights), heavy pointer dereferencing and a small set of global list heads (IGV's global indirection is cheap and disrupts static identification of list state, so it is strongly weighted), and frequent node/next traversals that ICALL can convert into analysis-resistant indirect calls at modest runtime cost. SPLIT and IBR diversify control flow cheaply-to-moderately and are kept active to raise structural diversity without dominating the hot loops. FLA is heavily penalized via a high RuntimeCost weight (control-flow flattening on the benchmark's tight traversal loops typically costs double-digit runtime overhead for limited marginal security beyond BCF+IBR) and is effectively restricted to any few features that strongly favor it; BCF gets moderate weights since its bogus-block size/runtime bloat hurts a small, cache-sensitive benchmark if over-applied. All passes use low CorrectnessRisk weights because these transformations are semantics-preserving on this workload's simple arithmetic, pointer, and loop constructs, with FLA and IBR slightly higher to steer those passes away from irregular pointer-driven control flow where misapplied flattening or branch rerouting carries the most risk.
